summary: Meta announced that Meta AI, powered by the previously released Muse Spark 1.1 model, now gains agentic features that let it plan multi-step tasks, connect to email and calendar apps, create slides and mood boards, and follow through on delegated tasks without re-prompting, rolling out first in select markets.

mechanisms.reason: Meta AI is described as executing delegated multi-step tasks autonomously rather than just responding to prompts, shifting work from user action to agent execution.
mechanisms.quote: Meta AI can now make plans, follow through on next steps, and keep you on track without needing to be reminded or re-prompted.

mechanisms.reason: Autonomous multi-step task handling (research, planning, scheduling, mood boards) implies more calls per task than a single-turn query, though no volume figures are given.
mechanisms.quote: You only have to set up tasks with Meta AI once, then you can leave Meta AI to handle them, whether that’s a weekly meal plan, a heads-up on the latest sneaker drops, or an afternoon update on trends you care about.

practices.reason: The underlying model's ability to plan, call external apps and follow through end-to-end is stated plainly but as a consumer product feature rather than a developer-facing capability an engineering team could adopt.
practices.quote: The model is built to plan, work with your apps, and follow through from start to finish, and those capabilities are what make the new features possible in Meta AI .
